players.product: vacuum valves and motion modules for deposition / etch chambers

quarterly_data.signal: Q3 2026 trading update (CFO Fabian Chiozza): Q3 sales of CHF 376 million, up 29% sequentially and up 46% year-on-year.
quarterly_data.figure: Q3 sales CHF 376 million, up 29% sequentially and up 46% year-on-year

quarterly_data.signal: Orders (CFO): order volumes tripled in Q3 compared to a year ago, reaching record levels (following the Q2 2026 record) as new production capacity for leading-edge semiconductors remains highly sought after; substantially ahead of VAT's own expectations, having indicated a flat order pattern for Q3 at the half-year call. Orders are predominantly from core semiconductor customers, driven by the continued supply-demand imbalance for advanced semiconductors, which is expected to last well into 2027. CFO: 'We are not seeing double bookings, but orders that are driven by real capacity demand.' He would assume customers are now also placing orders as they see demand for their tools building, and VAT is still receiving quite some reconfigurations, pointing at reprioritization in their demand.

Backlog (CFO): the book-to-bill ratio increased to around 1.9 times and the order backlog sits at CHF 980 million, an increase of 280% compared to the order book last year — 'testament to the unprecedented and unexpected steepness of the increase in demand'.
quarterly_data.figure: book-to-bill around 1.9 times; order backlog CHF 980 million, up 280% year-on-year

quarterly_data.signal: Lead times (CFO): order lead times have further lengthened during the year and currently extend to approximately nine months or more, versus as little as three months at the beginning of the year, giving better visibility of customer needs and helping plan manufacturing capacity and supplier demand. Customers claim visibility across the sector spanning the next eight quarters; VAT has very good visibility for the next six to eight quarters ahead.
quarterly_data.figure: order lead times approximately nine months or more (as little as three months at the beginning of the year)

quarterly_data.signal: Plant utilization (CFO): in Switzerland, assembly utilization has increased to more than 75% while the factory layout and workflows are further optimized; in Malaysia, utilization has reached over 90% (Malaysia 1A running at above 90% utilization). VAT added an additional 450 FTEs in Q3 globally, bringing the global workforce to around 4,500 FTEs, and is aligning the supplier base for continued growth into 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: Switzerland assembly utilization more than 75%; Malaysia utilization over 90%; workforce around 4,500 FTEs (450 added in Q3)

quarterly_data.signal: Malaysia expansion (CFO): VAT will ramp production further by bringing factory 1B online during the first quarter of 2027, the next step toward the planned manufacturing capacity of up to 1.2 billion at the site; overall Malaysia capacity including 1A and 1B amounts to more than CHF 1.2 billion. VAT is on track with its internal targets to add about 30% quarter-over-quarter overall, and Malaysia is clearly ahead of this and plays a pivotal role in the ramp; the Switzerland ramp is less accentuated but meeting targeted levels.
quarterly_data.figure: Malaysia factory 1B online in Q1 2027; Malaysia capacity (1A and 1B) more than CHF 1.2 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Romania (CFO): VAT is advancing the Arad site from a semi-finished goods operation to a fully integrated manufacturing location; finished products will be shipped directly from Arad to customers worldwide, increasing the site's contribution to total factory output by approximately CHF 200 million to CHF 300 million.
quarterly_data.figure: Arad contribution to total factory output up by approximately CHF 200 million to CHF 300 million

quarterly_data.signal: Global capacity (CFO): VAT is ramping toward a global footprint capacity of approximately CHF 2.5 billion (the current footprint provides around CHF 2.4 billion-CHF 2.7 billion of capacity) and has identified additional levers to expand beyond this. VAT originally thought this capacity would take it into 2030; with today's demand momentum it will need to take the next capacity decision earlier than initially anticipated and is assessing further expansions beyond the existing brick and mortar, including additional buildings. Lead time for such additions outside Switzerland is around 12 months plus qualification, up to 18 months; an update on the longer-term manufacturing roadmap is expected during 2027.
quarterly_data.figure: global footprint capacity approximately CHF 2.5 billion (around CHF 2.4 billion-CHF 2.7 billion); new capacity lead time up to 18 months

quarterly_data.signal: Factory output ramp (CFO): factory output delivered another quarter with a sequential 30% growth, and VAT is on track to achieve a quarterly output run rate of around CHF 450 million by end of 2026 and expects to ramp further; growth in factory output will continue, but most likely not at the 30% quarter-over-quarter seen at the beginning of the ramp, with the usual seasonal effects in Q1 around Chinese New Year. Q4 sales are affected by fewer production and shipping days around the holidays and by deliberate rebuilding of consignment inventory ahead of 2027. CFO expects revenues to keep growing into Q1 and progressively throughout 2027, and a strong Q1 despite Chinese New Year.
quarterly_data.figure: quarterly output run rate of around CHF 450 million by end of 2026

quarterly_data.signal: Guidance (CFO): Q4 2026 sales expected in the range of CHF 420 million-CHF 450 million; 2026 expected to be another record year for orders, sales and free cash flow, with higher EBITDA margin and net income compared with 2025. For 2027, VAT is preparing for a sales volume significantly above the previously communicated guidance of CHF 1.5 billion-CHF 1.7 billion. Normalizing for the extended order windows seen in Q3, CFO expects Q4 orders to land somewhere between CHF 500 million to CHF 600 million, a plateau that seems to repeat as per current indications of customer build plans. Guidance is based on the year-to-date average rate of $0.8 over CHF.
quarterly_data.figure: Q4 2026 sales CHF 420 million-CHF 450 million; Q4 orders CHF 500 million to CHF 600 million; 2027 sales significantly above CHF 1.5 billion-CHF 1.7 billion

quarterly_data.signal: Segments (CFO): in the semiconductors unit, Q3 orders were up 37% sequentially and 270% year-on-year and sales up 39% and 70% respectively, reflecting capacity ramp activities. In advanced industrials, order growth came from valves used in scientific instruments and analytical products and systems with exposure to semiconductors, while coatings and industrials saw flat year-on-year orders. In global service, orders increased 52% sequentially and 88% year-on-year as demand surged for consumables amid high utilization rates, with repairs and retrofits also up strongly; sales increased by only 2% sequentially and 4% year-on-year because many fab customers are maximizing output and limiting tool downtime for maintenance or upgrades.
quarterly_data.figure: semiconductors orders +37% QoQ / +270% YoY, sales +39% / +70%; global service orders +52% QoQ / +88% YoY, sales +2% / +4%

quarterly_data.signal: Service outlook (CFO, confirming an analyst's assumption that service growth will continue to pick up further in 2027 onwards): the service business will benefit from an ever-growing installed base, continuously strong demand for upgrade retrofits and the consumables business serving high fab utilization; he sees the service order pattern observed in Q3 as idiosyncratic and not a concern for the midterm growth trajectory of the service business.

Gross margin (CFO): the gross profit margin has gradually increased to around 65%-66% levels amid a series of negative effects; continuous improvement programs and the further ramp of production outside Switzerland bring positive contribution, and price increases merely compensate material and labor inflation, transportation and energy cost spikes. He would assume the gross profit margin will hover somewhere around 66% going forward. VAT is adding significant resources ahead of the growth opportunity, with new employees' productivity progressively increasing as the ramp matures, alongside efficiency programs.
quarterly_data.figure: gross profit margin around 65%-66%; expected to hover around 66% going forward

quarterly_data.signal: Pricing (CFO): VAT's pricing is value-based and not automatically increased because customers do so; it reflects technological value, new product introductions; certain input cost inflation (transportation, raw materials) is passed through. Prices for custom valves are constantly adjusted or set when new products are introduced; catalog parts (mostly advanced industrials) and some service products are repriced toward year-end, communicated in autumn and effective at the beginning of the year. Historically price announcements brought some uptick in order momentum, but the key growth driver remains fundamental demand.

China (CFO): China continues to develop in line with expectations; Q3 Chinese orders were slightly above the roughly 30% revenue share of China ('slightly above means low single-digit percentage'). VAT's strategy remains to work closely with OEMs, co-develop technologies and win the relevant specifications.
quarterly_data.figure: China orders slightly above the roughly 30% China sales share

quarterly_data.signal: Market view (CFO): about 150 fabs are under construction or planned over the next three years to address the persisting supply-demand imbalance; assuming each fab requires on average more than $10 billion US of WFE, the industry is well on track to seeing WFE growing to over $200 billion US per year in the years to come. VAT's internal projections point to about $200 billion for next year and somewhere around $250 billion to $260 billion for 2028 at the moment, the volume assumption currently used in its planning. CFO: 'AI is clearly accelerating demand, but the more fundamental trend is the continued advancement of semiconductor technology itself' (gate-all-around, sub-2 nanometer); fabs are being expanded and new ones brought online particularly in advanced logic and DRAM, with projects originally planned for later in the decade moving forward. On AI market fears, the demand outlook rests on semiconductor equipment customers' plans and direct customer conversations for 2027 and 2028, with confirmation from customers and end users that about 150 fabs are still going to be built.
quarterly_data.figure: about 150 fabs over the next three years; internal WFE projection about $200 billion for next year and $250 billion to $260 billion for 2028
